property_summary: For any caller with zero prior tokenBalance, calling airDrop increases that caller's tokenBalance by exactly 20 in the correct contract; the mutant that adds 40 will violate this (some input callers will observe a different resulting balance).

After any single external airDrop call by an address A that initially has zero tokenBalance, the reference contract ensures tokenBalance[A] increases by exactly 20 and no other account's tokenBalance changes; the mutant that removes the reentrancy lock can be re-entered by a malicious caller which causes tokenBalance for some address (possibly different from the caller) to differ after the call.

For every caller and adversary contract address, a single call to airDrop from an address with zero balance increases only that caller's tokenBalance by exactly 20 in the reference (due to reentrancy lock), whereas removing the lock allows a reentrant attacker to cause tokenBalance for some other key to change during the same call.

For every caller address A and for any adversarial attacker contract Addr that pretends to support the token, a single call c.airDrop() from A when tokenBalance[A]==0 leaves all other accounts' tokenBalance unchanged in the correct contract (only A's balance increments by 20); removing the reentrancy lock allows a reentrant attacker to make some other account's tokenBalance change during that same call.

For every caller address A with tokenBalance[A]==0 and for every attacker contract Addr that reports support for the token, a single call to c.airDrop() from A always leaves tokenBalance[Addr] unchanged in the reference (the reentrancy lock prevents the attacker from causing balances of other addresses to change); removing the reentrancy lock allows a reentrant attacker to change tokenBalance[Addr] during the same airDrop call.

For every caller address A with initial tokenBalance[A]==0, a single call to airDrop() on the correct contract always leaves every other account's tokenBalance unchanged (only A's balance increases by 20); removing the reentrancy lock allows a malicious callee (that re-enters) to change some other account's tokenBalance during the same call.

For every caller address a, invoking airDrop from a on the correct contract always increases tokenBalance(a) by 20 (from 0 to 20) when they start with zero balance; the mutant that demands a different token string will block such calls for callers that rely on Bank.supportsToken and thus will not increase that caller's tokenBalance for some caller addresses.

For any caller addr, after calling airDrop from that addr (with Bank(msg.sender) supporting the token), the reference contract always increases tokenBalance(addr) by exactly 20 when the caller had zero prior balance; the mutant inverts the hasNoBalance check and therefore will only allow the airdrop when caller already has non-zero balance, so there exist inputs (a caller with zero prior balance) for which tokenBalance(addr) differs between reference and mutant.

For any caller address, the reference contract always allows an airDrop to increase that caller's tokenBalance by 20 when their prior balance is zero; the mutant inverts the hasNoBalance check and denies callers with zero balance, so there exist callers (with zero prior balance) for which tokenBalance differs between reference and mutant after airDrop.

For any caller, a single call to airDrop() increases that caller's tokenBalance by exactly 20 in the reference contract; the mutant that adds 10 will cause tokenBalance to be less than 20 for some caller (breaking the rule).

For any caller with zero initial balance who passes supportsToken check, a single successful call to airDrop increases their tokenBalance by exactly 20 in the reference; the mutant that adds 10 will make the post-call balance != 20 for some caller, so asserting the balance equals 20 distinguishes them.

For any caller address that starts with byte 0x47 (i.e., first byte equals 0x47) and has zero initial tokenBalance and whose supportsToken() returns the correct marker, a successful airDrop call increases that caller's tokenBalance by 20 in the reference; the mutant that adds 10 will produce a post-call balance different from 20 for some such fuzzed caller.

For any caller, after a single call to airDrop the caller's tokenBalance increases by exactly 20 (no more, no less); the mutated modifier that flips the lock boolean allows reentrant calls to increment more than 20, violating this invariant for some attacker caller.

For any caller that starts with zero tokenBalance and calls airDrop, the reference contract never lets the caller reenter during airDrop so after the call tokenBalance == 20; the buggy modifier unlocking before the body allows a reentrant attacker to call back and achieve tokenBalance > 20 for some attacker address.

For every caller address that starts with zero tokenBalance, a single call to airDrop on the correct contract results in tokenBalance == 20 because reentrancy is blocked; the mutant unlocks before the body allowing a reentrant attacker to call back and obtain tokenBalance > 20 for some attacker address.

For every caller address, if that caller's tokenBalance starts at 0 and the caller's supportsToken() implementation reenters during airDrop to attempt a second airDrop, the reference contract prevents reentrancy so the final tokenBalance is exactly 20, whereas the mutant that unlocks early can be reentered and end up with tokenBalance > 20 for some attacker address.

For every caller address that begins with zero tokenBalance and whose supportsToken() returns the expected bytes32, a single external call to airDrop never allows a nested reentrant second call (the reference's modifier keeps _locked true across the call so final tokenBalance == 20); the mutant that flips the lock allows an attacker helper that reenters during supportsToken() to increase tokenBalance > 20 for some fuzzed attacker address.
